newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dana Petroleum awarded new licence off Ghana.
newsitem.headline: Dana Petroleum awarded new licence off Ghana.

text.p: Dana Petroleum plc said on Monday that its unit, Dana Petroleum (Ghana) Ltd, had been granted an exploration licence by the Ghanaian government and the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC).
Dana, who has a 45 percent interest in and is operator of, the contract area, said the agreement was expected to be ratified by the government during the next three months.
Dana's partners are Seafield Resources plc with a 45 percent interest and GNPC who has a 10 percent stake in the area, the group said in a statement.
"The Agreement provides for the exploration, development and production of petroleum in a contract area of 2,341 square kilometres offshore western Ghana, the statement said.

The Dana contract area is located over the continental shelf, slope and deep water of the Western Tano Basin, immediately adjacent to the Ivory Coast border, in the Gulf of Guinea of West Africa, it said.

Dana said the nearby Ivory Coast offshore area had enjoyed considerable exploration and development success for Cretaceous reservoirs in the last two years and similar geological conditions were thought to extend into the Ghana offshore area, including the contract area.
"The group has already identified a number of geological features and seismic will be acquired and processed in 1997 followed by a drilling programme, Dana said.
It said it also expected to benefit from infrastructure created by the planned development of the South Tano Oil and Gas Field currently operated by GNPC and surrounded by the contract area.
As part of this development, a gas fired power station is planned to be constructed on the coast some 20 km north of the contract area, it said.
